title: Exposure Matrix Canvas for Multi-Variant Progressive Ramp
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Operators lack a compact way to plan progressive exposure across multiple variants and cohorts that surface expected latency/cost and rollback boundaries. Goal: Design an interactive Exposure Matrix Canvas that lets SREs and PMs compose multi-variant ramps (eg. canary + A/B variant) visually, simulate telemetry impact, and generate a rollback/playbook snippet. The canvas should integrate with rollout policies, support saving templates, and present cost/latency delta estimates per cell.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas allows adding up to 6 cohorts and up to 4 variants per cohort
Each matrix cell can be edited for percent exposure and has inline expected token-cost and p50 latency delta estimates
Simulation mode shows projected traffic shift timeline and highlights cells breaching defined SLO thresholds
Export generates a JSON rollout spec compatible with the rollout engine and a copyable emergency rollback script
Prototype validated with 3 internal PM/Eng reviewers and one customer-facing pilot team
decisions: Use a two-dimensional matrix (cohorts x variants) rather than timeline-only UI to make combinatorial exposure clearer
Inline cost/latency estimates will be precomputed for the common sequence-length distributions to avoid runtime stalls
Cells can be pinned for continuous KV-caching eligibility; pinned cells are visually emphasized and factored into cost estimates
Simulation will run on sampled telemetry with a configurable horizon (1m, 5m, 1h) and surface risk flags for breach probability > 5%
mockup_notes: Top bar: project selector + quick-sim toggle + 'generate spec' action
Left axis: cohort list with audience filters and sample size estimator
Top axis: variant cards with model variant, quantization profile, and estimated tokens/sec
Cells: editable exposure slider, inline micro-chart of recent latency, small badge for cost delta
Right rail: live simulation timeline, SLO breach heatmap, and rollback quick-actions
Footer: save template, share link, and 'preview rollout in staging' button
reviewers_feedback: Rohit Desai (Eng): Request adding a dependency indicator when a variant requires a fallback model; flagged simulation accuracy assumptions
Maya Patel (PM): Likes matrix compactness; asked for clearer labelling when cohorts overlap (audience intersection warnings)
Jonas Eriksson (SRE): Suggests defaulting to conservative cache eligibility if the cohort size is < 1% of traffic
Product Design Review: Prefer color scale for risk, but require a patterned fill option for accessibility/color-blind palette
next_steps: Iterate prototype with engineering notes on where precompute is required (ETA 1 week)

Add fallback-model dependency visualization and update Figma frames
